In every pair, A is the weaker image, and the four A frames share the same defects. The character is the main problem: smooth, doll-like faces with blotchy low-resolution skin; hair as one solid mass; repeated black square texture artifacts on the arms; a stair-stepped shirt hem; mitten-like hands that never actually grip the pistol (the two-handed aim in pair 2 is the worst case); plaid and denim with no folds; and arms-hanging idle poses. The surroundings add to it: shopfronts with black empty interiors and placeholder signs, and the character does not pick up the warm backlight. A's strongest frame is the street gameplay view in pair 3, where the warm daylight and dappled tree shadows are genuinely attractive. Even there, sparse pedestrians and traffic, blurry building textures and a placeholder minimap keep it well below B's busy street. Every B frame combines a detailed face, real cloth folds, a believable grip on the prop, a pose that tells a story and a rich, lived-in setting. To close the gap, the A team should fix the following, highest leverage first: (1) hand and finger posing on weapons; (2) skin and face material and textures; (3) remove the arm artifacts and the stair-stepped hem; (4) add real cloth folds; (5) populate shop interiors and raise the number of pedestrians and vehicles. None of the A frames impressed me.
